name: George Austin
bio: George Austin is a Republican candidate for Connecticut's 2nd Congressional District from Suffield. He grew up in the construction trade, studied construction management at Central Connecticut State University and has run a contracting business in eastern Connecticut. He is the son of an immigrant from Mexico.

platform.point: Cut wasteful federal spending with a household-budget approach to taxpayer money.
Shore up Social Security and Medicare so they stay solvent for current and future retirees.
Lower taxes and regulations and widen access to homeownership for working families.
Improve VA services and the quality of care veterans receive.
Set guardrails on AI so its gains reach American workers rather than only large tech firms.
Protect the unborn and defend Second Amendment rights.

economy.evidence: Campaign calls for lower taxes, fewer regulations and cuts to government waste.

liberty.evidence: Averages opposition to abortion (community norms) with defense of Second Amendment gun rights (individual choice).

tech.evidence: Calls for AI guardrails so innovation benefits workers and not just tech monopolies.

notes: Little detail is published on his specific legislative proposals; liberty score rests on convention coverage of his abortion and gun stances.

name: Rosa DeLauro
bio: Rosa DeLauro has represented Connecticut's 3rd District since 1991 and is the top Democrat on the House Appropriations Committee, which she chaired from 2021 to 2023. Before Congress she was chief of staff to Senator Chris Dodd and executive director of EMILY's List. She was born in New Haven.

platform.point: Lower everyday costs for families in the district.
Expand health care access, including a public insurance option and negotiated drug prices.
Support quality public education and oppose private school vouchers.
Protect and strengthen benefits relied on by older residents.
Reassert Congress's control over federal spending decisions against the executive branch.
Strengthen federal food safety oversight, including a separate Food Safety Administration.

economy.evidence: Rated 100% by Citizens for Tax Justice for progressive taxation and opposed making the Bush tax cuts permanent.

welfare.evidence: Calls health care a right and backs a public insurance option.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights, LGBTQ rights and drug-policy reform, while backing stricter gun rules such as universal background checks.

security.evidence: Voted against removing the FISA warrant requirement for wiretapping and backs limits on domestic call monitoring.

immigration.evidence: Backs a path to citizenship and higher visa caps and opposes a border wall; opposed more ICE funding but not abolishing ICE.

energy.evidence: Supports the Green New Deal and 50% clean electricity by 2030, and opposes offshore drilling.

education.evidence: Opposes private and religious school vouchers; rated 100% by the NEA.

faith.evidence: Voted to let courts rule on 'under God' in the Pledge, opposing a bar on judicial review.

notes: Liberty and immigration scores kept from earlier research although her record could support somewhat lower values.

name: Christopher Lancia
current_role: Fiber network manager and former federal law enforcement officer
bio: Christopher Lancia is the Republican nominee for Connecticut's 3rd District and lives in Milford; he was born and raised in Bridgeport. He is a U.S. Coast Guard veteran and former federal law enforcement officer who now manages outside plant operations at a fiber network company. He holds a bachelor's degree in emergency management from Post University.

platform.point: Secure the border, treating it as a national security issue tied to crime and drugs.
Keep decisions about children with parents and bar transgender women from women's sports.
Fight inflation with lower taxes and balanced budgets.
Enact congressional term limits and end what he calls weaponization of government.
Back law enforcement and Second Amendment rights.

economy.evidence: Campaigns on lower taxes and balanced budgets.

liberty.evidence: Averages opposition to transgender women in women's sports with support for gun rights and opposition to vaccine mandates.

security.evidence: Campaign pledges support for law enforcement.

immigration.evidence: Calls border security national security and pledges to end border chaos.

education.evidence: Backs parental rights and parent-led decisions for children.

name: Thomas Egan
bio: Thomas Egan is an attorney from Ansonia running for Connecticut's 3rd District on the Independent Party line. His practice includes suing insurance companies and pro bono work for tenants facing eviction. He has previously run for mayor of Ansonia and for state representative.

platform.point: Let courts award attorney fees to people who win insurance benefit disputes, discouraging denial of valid claims.
Raise the federal minimum wage above $7.25 an hour.
Keep federal funding for rental assistance programs as evictions rise.
Turn a vacant Ansonia copper mill into a recycling, solar assembly and high-tech manufacturing site.
Expand high-speed rail.
Create a path to citizenship for undocumented residents already in the country.

economy.evidence: Supports raising the federal minimum wage and a federally backed manufacturing redevelopment.

welfare.evidence: Wants federal rental assistance funding maintained.

immigration.evidence: Supports a citizenship path for undocumented residents.

energy.evidence: Proposes solar assembly manufacturing and more high-speed rail.

notes: No campaign website was found; profile relies on one New Haven Independent report.

name: Jim Himes
bio: Jim Himes has represented Connecticut's 4th District since 2009 and has served as the top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee. Before Congress he worked at Goldman Sachs and led a nonprofit affordable housing lender in New York, and served on Greenwich local boards. He was born in Lima, Peru, and is a Harvard graduate and Rhodes Scholar.

platform.point: Close the gun show loophole and ban large-capacity magazines.
Protect the Affordable Care Act, Medicare and Medicaid while reining in costs.
Use financial incentives and research funding to cut emissions while meeting energy needs.
Protect access to abortion.
Pass comprehensive reform with an earned path to citizenship.
Make economic growth reach workers across income levels.

economy.evidence: Voted against a 2022 antitrust merger-fee package and for a 2025 resolution condemning socialism, while backing higher estate taxes.

welfare.evidence: Supports expanding the ACA with a basic coverage plan and opposes Medicare privatization.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights, LGBTQ protections and drug-policy reform, while backing strict gun regulation.

security.evidence: Supported the 2026 FISA Section 702 renewal and voted against defunding NSA phone metadata collection.

immigration.evidence: Backs comprehensive reform with an earned path to citizenship and the DREAM Act.

foreign.evidence: Supports Iran sanctions and a strong U.S.-Israel bond; member of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus.

energy.evidence: Voted for the American Clean Energy and Security Act and supports regulating greenhouse gases.

tech.evidence: Voted against the 2022 antitrust merger-fee package, though he backs net neutrality.

education.evidence: Opposes school vouchers and voted to double Early Head Start funding.

name: Michael Goldstein
bio: Michael Goldstein is a surgeon and lawyer from Greenwich who owns a medical practice and twice served as president of the New York County Medical Society. He was the Republican nominee for Connecticut's 4th District in 2024 and also ran for the seat in 2020 and 2022.

platform.point: Reduce health care regulation to increase competition and expand Right to Try access to experimental treatments.
Expand natural gas pipeline capacity into New England, alongside nuclear and renewables, to cut electricity rates.
Promote school choice, vocational training and apprenticeships with Connecticut employers.
Ban gender-affirming surgery for minors.
Oppose unchecked federal spending, hiring quotas and critical race theory.

economy.evidence: Opposes unchecked federal spending and favors deregulation to lower health costs.

welfare.evidence: Says lower health costs require less government involvement, not more.

liberty.evidence: Averages support for Second Amendment rights with a ban on gender-affirming surgery for minors.

energy.evidence: Prioritizes new natural gas pipelines while also supporting nuclear and renewables.

name: Jahana Hayes
bio: Jahana Hayes has represented Connecticut's 5th District since 2019 and is ranking member of the House Agriculture subcommittee on nutrition and foreign agriculture. She previously taught history in Waterbury public schools and was named 2016 National Teacher of the Year. She was born and raised in Waterbury.

platform.point: Back Medicare for All and cap prescription drug costs.
Expand access to nutritious food so no American goes hungry.
Ensure every child has access to an excellent public education.
Pass red flag laws, expanded background checks, buybacks and a higher purchase age for certain guns.
Pass the PRO Act to strengthen workers' right to organize.
Expand first-time homebuyer assistance and grants.

economy.evidence: Seeks an economy that works for all, not just the ultra-wealthy, and backs the PRO Act.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion access and LGBTQ equality, while backing red flag laws and universal background checks.

immigration.evidence: Supports a path to citizenship and higher visa caps.

education.evidence: Opposes school vouchers and prioritizes public education.

name: Chris Shea
bio: Chris Shea is a lieutenant with the North Haven Fire Department and a retired Navy SEAL with more than 30 years of service, including a Pentagon assignment on special warfare budgets. He founded Hero to Hero, a nonprofit helping veterans become first responders, and once ran a handyman business. A Watertown native who lives in Cheshire, he won the August 2026 Republican primary for Connecticut's 5th District.

platform.point: Lower energy costs and the tax burden and remove barriers that raise housing costs.
Pursue pro-worker, pro-business policies and fight overregulation.
Secure the border, enforce immigration laws and stop fentanyl trafficking.
Maintain military strength and readiness and support Israel's right to self-defense.
Improve VA access and create first-responder career paths for departing service members.
Defend parental rights and oppose what he calls woke ideologies in schools.

economy.evidence: Pledges to fight overregulation and reduce the tax burden.

security.evidence: Campaign pledges support for law enforcement.

immigration.evidence: Calls for securing the border and enforcing immigration laws.

foreign.evidence: Backs strong military readiness and standing with Israel.

notes: Coverage lists Cheshire as his home town while his campaign site calls him a Watertown native.

name: Sarah McBride
current_role: U.S. Representative for Delaware's at-large district
bio: Sarah McBride has represented Delaware's at-large district since 2025 and is the first openly transgender member of Congress. She served in the Delaware Senate from 2020 to 2025, where she sponsored the state's paid family and medical leave law, and earlier worked as an LGBTQ rights advocate. She was born in Wilmington and graduated from American University.

platform.point: Move toward universal coverage with a public option, a lower Medicare age and added dental and vision benefits.
Guarantee paid sick time and paid family and medical leave.
Build on the Inflation Reduction Act to expand renewable energy and reach net-zero emissions.
Pass measures to reduce gun violence.
Protect access to reproductive health care.
Strengthen workers' rights and unions.

economy.evidence: Backs a working-families economy, stronger unions and a minimum wage increase.

welfare.evidence: Supports a public option, Medicare expansion and paid leave as steps toward universal coverage.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights, LGBTQ rights and marijuana decriminalization, while backing a ghost-gun ban.

foreign.evidence: Supports aid to Israel and Ukraine and joined a delegation backing Denmark amid the Greenland dispute.

energy.evidence: Wants more renewable investment building on the Inflation Reduction Act and net-zero emissions.

name: Joseph Arminio
bio: Joseph Arminio is a Wilmington native with a Ph.D. in political science from MIT and a bachelor's degree from Johns Hopkins. He chaired the National Coalition for Defense, taught at American University and Lincoln University, published a Maryland newspaper and has written several books on American policy and history. He ran in Maryland's 2008 Republican congressional primary.

platform.point: Adopt his American Prosperity Plan to address stagflation and high public and private debt.
End open-ended wars, avoid entanglement in Ukraine and Iran, and push Israel toward a two-state solution.
Require formal debate in high school and teach economic history from primary sources.
Uphold the Second Amendment and the full Constitution.
Enforce existing immigration law and end sanctuary cities.

liberty.evidence: Campaign pledges to uphold Second Amendment gun rights; other liberty issues not addressed.

immigration.evidence: Calls for enforcing immigration law and ending sanctuary cities.

foreign.evidence: Opposes endless wars and entanglements in Ukraine and Iran.

notes: Wikipedia's race page lists him as a medical doctor, but his campaign biography describes a political science Ph.D.; the campaign description is used here.

name: Robert White
current_role: At-large member of the Council of the District of Columbia
bio: Robert White has been an at-large member of the D.C. Council since 2016 and won the June 2026 Democratic primary for D.C. Delegate. He previously was legislative counsel to Delegate Eleanor Holmes Norton and community outreach director for D.C. Attorney General Karl Racine, and ran for mayor in 2022. A Washington native, he holds a law degree from American University.

platform.point: Build local and national coalitions to pass D.C. statehood.
Secure federal resources for affordable housing and workforce training for residents without college degrees.
Pair accountability for serious crimes with youth programs that address causes of crime.
Resist federal interference in D.C. governance and budgets, including ICE operations.
Seek federal payments to offset the impact of federal workforce cuts on the region.
Push for federal funding for teachers, classrooms and workforce readiness.

welfare.evidence: Passed the Birth to Three for All DC Act expanding early childhood programs.

immigration.evidence: Campaign pledges to protect D.C. from ICE operations.

energy.evidence: Championed the Renewable Energy Future Amendment Act on the D.C. Council.

education.evidence: Seeks more federal funding for teachers and classrooms.

notes: The Commons portrait is credited to the D.C. Council with a public-domain claim that is uncertain for local government works, so it was not used.

name: Denise Rosado
bio: Denise Rosado is an attorney and former attorney advisor at the Federal Communications Commission who has also served as an Arizona assistant attorney general and an administrative law judge. Her earlier work includes roles at the Commerce Department and Census Bureau and teaching in New York City. Born in Paterson, New Jersey, she moved to Washington in 2004.

platform.point: Coordinate with federal law enforcement to reduce crime and publish accurate crime statistics.
Require third-grade reading and writing proficiency before promotion, with intensive help for struggling students.
Exempt D.C. residents from federal income tax while the District lacks a voting member of Congress.
Convert vacant buildings into homes and streamline development approvals.
End automated photo-enforcement tickets.
Make D.C. a hub for technology and AI innovation.

liberty.evidence: Averages support for gun rights with backing for women's sports limits, a ban on transition surgery for minors and classroom limits on gender topics.

security.evidence: Supports tougher public safety policy and closer coordination with federal law enforcement.

tech.evidence: Wants D.C. to become a hub for technology and AI innovation.

education.evidence: Backs parental rights and age-appropriate limits on classroom discussion of sexual orientation and gender identity.

notes: Tech score rests only on her pro-innovation framing, with no stated position on AI regulation.
